newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fujitsu Australia posts modest annual profit.
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu Australia posts modest annual profit.

text.p: The Australian subsidiary of Japan-based electronics, computer and telecommunications giant Fujitsu Ltd said on Monday that it had posted a "modest" net profit for the year to March 31.
Fujitsu Australia chairman Neville Roach said the company recorded a net profit for the year of A$600,000 after 11.5 percent growth in consolidated revenue to A$734 million.
"While our profit was modest, we are pleased to have remained profitable in a very difficult environment as far as margins are concerned," Roach said in a statement.

"This means that we have now been profitable for 14 out of the past 15 years despite having to manage continuous restructuring of our business necessitated by the dramatic changes in our industry," Roach said.
Fujitsu Ltd owns 80 percent of the Australian company. Its U.K.-based subsidiary, ICL, holds the other 20 percent.

The A$734 consolidated revenue figure took into account the A$86 million revenue divested when Fujistu Australia sold its interest in the Axicorp and Pyramid joint ventures at the end of the previous year.
